claude.sample_unit: women (screening examinations; 11,998 AI-supported and 11,998 matched historical controls)

links.outcome: Cancer detection, recall rate, PPV with AI as concurrent reading support vs without
links.effect: CDR 9.0‰ vs 5.8‰ (+3.2‰, p<0.001); PPV 14.6% vs 10.6% (+4%, p<0.001); recall rate 6.1% vs 5.4% (+0.7%, p<0.001); radiologists made final recall decision.
links.quote: The implementation of an AI system for concurrent decision support for reading DM and DBT screening exams increased the breast cancer detection rate (CDR) by 3.2‰ (9.0‰ vs 5.8‰; p < 0.001) and the positive predictive value (PPV) of the recalled women by 4% (14.6% vs 10.6%; p < 0.001) with an acceptable increase in recall rate (RR) by 0.7% (6.1% vs 5.4%; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Cancer detection rate, recall rate, and positive predictive value of recalls
links.effect: With versus without AI: CDR 9.0‰ vs 5.8‰; PPV 14.6% vs 10.6%; recall rate 6.1% vs 5.4% (all p < 0.001).
links.quote: The implementation of an AI system for concurrent decision support for reading DM and DBT screening exams increased the breast cancer detection rate (CDR) by 3.2‰ (9.0‰ vs 5.8‰; p < 0.001) and the positive predictive value (PPV) of the recalled women by 4% (14.6% vs 10.6%; p < 0.001) with an acceptable increase in recall rate (RR) by 0.7% (6.1% vs 5.4%; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Detected cancers assigned low risk by AI
links.effect: Among 108 detected cancers, AI categorized 1 (0.9%) as low risk, 32 (29.6%) as intermediate, and 75 (69.4%) as elevated.
links.quote: The 108 studies with cancers were categorized as follows: low, 1 (0.9%); intermediate, 32 (29.6%); elevated, 75 (69.4%) (Fig. 4 ).

links.outcome: cancer detection rate, recall rate, and PPV
links.effect: AI support increased CDR by 3.2/‰, PPV by 4%, and recall rate by 0.7% compared to reading without AI.
links.quote: Comparing global results (including DM and DBT) of double reading with vs. without AI support, we observed an increase in CDR, PPV, and RR by 3.2/‰ (5.8 vs. 9; p < 0.001), 4% (10.6 vs. 14.6; p < 0.001), and 0.7% (5.4 vs. 6.1; p < 0.001) respectively.

screen.practice: concurrent AI decision support for human double reading
screen.reason: The study evaluates a real-life clinical deployment of AI decision support integrated into human double-reading screening compared to standard double reading without AI.
